newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks lead Greek shares lower, approach 1,500pts.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead Greek shares lower, approach 1,500pts.

text.p: Greek shares were led 1.48 percent lower on Friday by weakness in banking stocks which brokers attributed to position squaring and profit-taking ahead of the weekend and the Albanian elections.

"Banks have led market trends throughout this year and fell pray today to position squaring ahead of the weekend and liquidations against Sunday's election in Albania," said Alexandros Papadopoulos, broker at EuroSec.
Albania will hold general elections on June 29 amidst continuing anarchy and gangster feuds after the collapse of financial pyramid scemes earlier this year.
"Banks suffered the most because they offer large scope for profit-taking following their outperformance of this year's rally," Papadopoulos said.
"Other sectors are less volatile as trading volume in those stocks is thinner and simply try to follow banks," he added.
The market was seen consolidating after the part-flotation of OTE telecom which was completed around mid-June with investors awaiting for the next leg of the rally.
"Following the part-flotation of OTE telecom the market has been trying to steady itself and some investors stayed on the sidelines awaiting for the market to head higher," said Papadopoulos.
"There is no doubt they will re-enter the market as there are no satisfactory alternative investments around," he added.
The Athens general index softened 1.48 percent or 22.67 points to 1,507.67 from Thursday's 1,530.34 near the day's low of 1,504.29.
Banks led the market lower with a 2.55 percent drop, while other sectors closed with mild gains only.

Turnover was boosted to 37.5 billion drachmas on volume of 6.0 million shares by active block trading which included National Bank, total 361,000 shares which changed hands at around 34,220-34,400 drachmas, and Intracom, 16,000 shares at 13,300.
Decliners beat advancers 134 to 89 with 23 shares unchanged on 246 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.30-$11.70. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,102-1,132 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,051-1,111 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument lost 95 drachmas to 6,205.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 524.92-558.43 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $66.12-$67.81. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 2,888-3,099 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $10.12-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 193-223 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
